global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredients available across all candidate recipes — i.e., the size of the ingredient universe. Used to understand the full range of ingredient identifiers and to check ingredient conflicts when building a menu.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate recipes the chef is considering for tonight. This is the count of recipe entries that follow.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single recipe. Refer to this id when selecting or listing recipes for the menu.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of ingredient identifiers used by this recipe. Ingredients listed here are the resources that cannot be shared with any other selected recipe (any overlap creates a conflict).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct community members who appear anywhere on the invitation lists — the size of the universe of possible guests.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed themed gatherings the committee has drafted (i.e., how many guest lists / candidate events are available to choose from).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single proposed gathering (e.g., an index or short label) used to reference that event when selecting which gatherings to hold.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The space-separated list of guest identifiers invited to that particular gathering; each identifier corresponds to a community member and no identifier may appear in more than one chosen gathering.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct garment items in the stylist's pool (the universe of pieces, e.g. 'jacket1', 'dress3'). Use this to know how many unique items exist overall.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate ensembles (ready-made looks) the stylist has prepared. This is how many possible outfits you can choose from.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or label for a specific ensemble/look (for example 'look1' or 'ensembleA'). Identifies which candidate outfit the following garment list belongs to.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated garment identifiers that make up this look (each identifier refers to an item from the pool). These are the items that would be reserved if this look is selected; no garment may appear in more than one chosen look.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct songs in the universe that the playlists are drawn from; used only to describe the size of the song pool available to the radio host.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of ready-to-go live playlists the host can choose from; this is the count of candidate sets the solver may select from.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single playlist (e.g., a name or numeric ID). This label uniquely names one ready-to-go live playlist that must be aired whole if chosen.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of song identifiers (titles or IDs) included in the playlist. Matching strings across playlists indicate the same song; any overlap means those playlists cannot both be selected because no track may appear in more than one chosen playlist.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plant species in the gardener's universe (the full pool of species that may appear in bed plans). This tells the solver how large the species pool is.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed planting schemes (bed plans) the gardener has stacked up. The solver's goal is to select as many of these plans as possible while keeping species disjoint.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single bed plan (one planting scheme). Use this id to refer to, select, or list chosen beds.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The space-separated list of plant species planted together in this bed plan. When choosing multiple bed plans, no species from these lists may appear in more than one selected bed.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct book titles in the library's universe that appear across all club proposals. This tells you how many unique elements (books) exist for checking overlaps between clubs.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed discussion clubs collected by the librarian. The scheduling goal is to select as many of these proposals as possible without any title being used by more than one chosen club.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific proposed discussion club (for example, an index or label). Use this to reference and list which clubs are selected in the final schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the book titles (or their identifiers) that this club plans to use. Two clubs conflict if their recommended_titles share any title, so selected clubs must have disjoint recommended_titles.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct staff members available across all proposed rosters — the size of the staff pool (the universe). Used to understand how many unique people exist when checking for overlaps between approved teams.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed project teams (rosters) submitted for approval. Each corresponds to one candidate roster the office manager can choose to approve.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this proposed team/roster. Refer to this id when selecting or reporting which rosters are approved.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for staff members on this proposed team. These are the people assigned to that roster; any member listed in more than one approved roster causes a conflict (so approved rosters must be disjoint in these ids).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct delivery addresses (stops) in the universe of all routes — i.e., how many unique stops exist across all route sheets.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of full routes (route sheets) available to choose from. This is the count of route entries you can select among.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier printed on a route sheet. Use this to refer to a specific full route when selecting or reporting chosen routes.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the delivery stops on this route sheet. Each token names a delivery address; chosen routes must not share any of these stop identifiers with one another.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct models available in the studio pool that appear across shoots; these are the individual people who cannot be double-booked.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed shoots (call sheets) you can choose from; the goal is to select as many of these shoots as possible without sharing models.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this shoot (call sheet), such as a name or index used to refer to the shoot when selecting lineups.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the models required for this shoot; none of these models may appear in more than one selected shoot.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct product types (the universe of product categories) that appear anywhere on the floor plan. This tells you how many unique element IDs exist across all booth pairings.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available booth pairings (candidate sets) that the organizer can approve. Each corresponds to one booth pairing option to choose from.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this specific booth pairing (the set). Use this ID to refer to the pairing when listing approved booths.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated product-type identifiers sold by this booth pairing. These are the elements of the set; no two approved pairings may share any of these product-type IDs.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct students in the counselor's pool (the universe of students). This tells how many unique students exist across all proposed study groups.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed study groups available to choose from. The goal is to accept as many of these proposals as possible subject to students not being shared between chosen groups.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a proposed study group (e.g., a label or number). Use this ID to refer to and select that specific group proposal.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the students (IDs or names) who would be in this proposed group. When scheduling, no student listed here may appear in more than one chosen group (chosen groups must be pairwise disjoint).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteers who signed up across all shifts. Count each volunteer only once; this defines the universe of people whose sign-ups create conflicts between shifts.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate shifts the coordinator can choose from. This is the number of available shift options (sets); the objective is to keep as many of these shifts open as possible subject to the volunteer-overlap restriction.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific candidate shift (for example a time label or numeric id). Use this id to name and select shifts when forming the final schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of volunteers (by name or unique volunteer id) who signed up for this shift. These are the people assigned to that shift; no volunteer listed here may appear on more than one chosen shift in the final schedule.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct artifacts in the museum's universe for this instance — i.e., how many different artifact identifiers exist across all described mini exhibits. Used to understand the pool of artifacts that must not be duplicated among selected exhibits.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available mini exhibits the curator can choose from. Each mini exhibit is a fixed group of artifacts; this count tells you how many such exhibit options are listed.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific mini exhibit option (e.g., a label or number). Solvers use this id to refer to and select complete exhibits; selecting an exhibit means placing this entire group of artifacts on the gallery floor.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated artifact identifiers that make up this mini exhibit. Each token is an artifact from the museum's universe; when an exhibit is selected, all listed artifacts are used and no listed artifact may appear in any other selected exhibit.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct speakers in the universe of proposals. This integer gives the size of the speaker pool from which all workshop speaker identifiers are drawn.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of workshop proposals available to schedule. This integer is the count of sets (workshops) the planner can choose from.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a workshop proposal (for example a number or code). Used to refer to that specific workshop when selecting the schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated speaker identifiers listed for this workshop. Each identifier names a speaker (an element of the universe); no speaker may appear in more than one selected workshop.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct vehicles available across all tour packages (i.e., the count of unique car IDs that appear in the input). This tells you how many individual cars the shop has to allocate and is the resource pool that cannot be double-assigned.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tour packages offered by the shop (i.e., how many different bundles are listed). This is the number of candidate bundles you can choose from to maximize the count of sellable packages.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific tour package (e.g., 'P1', '3', or any label). Use this to refer to that package when deciding which bundles to offer.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the vehicle identifiers required by this package (each identifier corresponds to a specific car). If two packages share any of these vehicle_ids they cannot both be selected because a vehicle cannot serve two chosen packages.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct students in the universe of all proposed sessions — i.e., how many unique student IDs exist across all session options. This is the size of the student pool the manager must ensure is assigned to at most one chosen session each.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed group lessons (session options) the manager can choose from. The objective is to schedule as many of these sessions as possible subject to the one-session-per-student rule.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single proposed group lesson (e.g., 'S1', '3', or any label). Use this ID to refer to and choose specific sessions in the schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of student IDs who would attend that particular session. Each token is a student from the universe; when selecting sessions, no two chosen sessions may include the same student ID.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct laboratory instruments available across the binder — i.e., the size of the universe of equipment items that configurations may require.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of experimental configurations listed in the supervisor's binder; the count of sets (each representing one complete experiment) that can potentially be prepared.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific experimental configuration in the binder; used to refer to and choose that complete setup for preparation.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of instrument identifiers required by this configuration. All listed instruments must be exclusively reserved for the configuration (no sharing) for it to be counted as prepared.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct films available across all proposed screening blocks (i.e., the size of the film universe). Use this to understand the universe of films that must not be double-booked.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed screening blocks the curator can choose from. The objective is to select as many of these blocks as possible without scheduling any film more than once.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (label or index) for a specific screening block proposal. Refer to this when selecting or listing chosen blocks.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of film identifiers (names or IDs) included in this block. These tokens indicate which films would be scheduled if the block is selected; no token may appear in more than one chosen block.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct food items across all possible picnic baskets — the size of the food-item universe the parent is avoiding duplicating.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of candidate picnic baskets the parent could give away. The objective is to choose as many of these baskets as possible without any food item appearing in more than one chosen basket.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single picnic basket (used to refer to that basket when selecting which to give away).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the food items contained in that basket (each token is a food type). Selected baskets must be pairwise disjoint in these food items so no item is duplicated across given baskets.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct accessories (bags, bracelets, hats, etc.) across all display proposals — the size of the universe of items the boutique can use when ensuring displays do not share any accessory.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of proposed window displays the boutique has suggested. The solver's objective is to choose as many of these proposals as possible without any overlap in accessories.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for one proposed window display (e.g., a proposal number or label) used to refer to that specific display option.

item_fields.name: elements

global_fields.name: num_elements

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The space-separated identifiers of the books that belong to this themed shelf idea. Each identifier names one book used by that shelf; when selecting shelves, no book identifier may appear in more than one chosen 'books_on_shelf' list.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct tracks in the curator's universe — i.e., the count of unique song identifiers available across all candidate playlists. This defines the universe size for checking whether playlists share tracks.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: set_id

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of track identifiers (IDs or normalized song titles) that belong to this playlist. These tokens are used to detect conflicts: no track token may appear in more than one selected playlist.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteers in the universe — count of all individual people who appear on any squad roster. Used to understand how many unique people are available across all squads.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: set_id

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The space-separated list of volunteers assigned to this squad (each volunteer represented by a name or ID). Squads that share any volunteer here cannot both be deployed.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct individual furniture pieces in the showroom inventory (the universe of items that appear across all bundles). This number counts unique piece identifiers used when evaluating that no piece is placed in more than one selected bundle.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: elements

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct machines in the plant (the size of the machine universe). Use this to understand how many different machines exist overall.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a production batch. Use this id to refer to and select specific batches to run.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of machine identifiers that this batch requires to run. No two selected batches may share any of these machine identifiers.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct students in the roster for the term. Use this to understand the size of the universe from which teams are formed and to verify that no student is counted more than once across approved teams.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pre-formed project teams the department sent. This is the number of team proposals you may choose from when approving as many non-overlapping teams as possible.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for one proposed project team (e.g., a number or short label). Use this to reference which specific team you approve or reject.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the students (by name or unique student ID) who belong to this proposed team. When selecting teams to approve, no student listed here may appear in more than one approved team.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct resources (models and props) available for the weekend. Each model or prop is counted once; this describes the size of the resource pool that packages draw from.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: set_id

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of resource identifiers (models and props) required by this package. These are the exact resources that must be reserved together if the package is chosen; no resource listed here may appear in more than one selected package.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct clothing items (garments and accessories) across all outfit combinations listed. This counts each unique item identifier once and defines the universe of items that cannot be reused between showcased outfits.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of outfit combinations the boutique can choose from for the window display. Each outfit is a candidate set that may be selected, subject to the rule that items cannot appear in more than one chosen outfit.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific outfit combination (e.g., O1, 3). Use this label to refer to that outfit when deciding which combinations to include in the window display.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers of the clothing items that compose the outfit (e.g., top1 skirt2 scarfA). These are the actual garments/accessories required for that outfit; when selecting outfits for display, no item identifier listed here may appear in more than one chosen outfit.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct speakers across all proposed panels. This defines the universe of speakers — no speaker may appear in more than one selected panel.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of panel sessions proposed for the event. The goal is to choose as many of these proposals as possible while respecting the speaker availability constraint.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific panel proposal (e.g., an alphanumeric code). Used to reference and count panels when forming the final schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated speaker identifiers (names or IDs) assigned to that panel. Any overlap in these identifiers between two panels creates a conflict, so selected panels must have disjoint speaker lists.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plant species across all submitted planting plans — i.e., the size of the universe of species that must not be duplicated among the chosen plans.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of planting plans (one per neighbor) available to choose from; this is the count of candidate plans you can select from.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single planting plan (for example a plan number or neighbor name) used to refer to that plan when selecting the final collection.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of plant species included in that planting plan. Each entry is a species (an element); chosen plans must be pairwise disjoint in these species so no species appears in more than one selected plan.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct products in the store's universe (across all bundles). Use this to understand the size of the product pool and to validate that product identifiers in bundles refer to items within this universe.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate promotional bundles the merchandiser can choose from. This is the count of bundle entries provided and helps frame how many choices must be considered when maximizing the number of non-overlapping bundles.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific promotional bundle (e.g., an index, SKU, or label). Use this id to refer to and report which bundles are selected.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated product identifiers that comprise the bundle. When selecting bundles, these products must not appear in more than one chosen bundle (i.e., chosen bundles must have pairwise disjoint product lists).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct athletes available on the roster (the universe of individuals referenced across all drills). This tells the solver how many unique athletes could appear in drill lists.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct practice drills available to choose from. The solver's aim is to pick as many of these drills as possible under the scheduling constraint.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or number) for a specific practice drill. Use this to refer to and report which drills are selected for the session.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of athlete identifiers who participate in this drill. If two chosen drills share any athlete from these lists, they conflict and only one of them may be scheduled.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct personal belongings across all packed boxes (the universe of items you must not duplicate in sealed boxes).

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of packed moving boxes available to consider sealing today.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific packed moving box (used to refer to that box when choosing which boxes to seal).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of personal belongings placed inside this box; when selecting boxes to seal, no item listed here may appear in more than one sealed box.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct influencers available for the season — i.e., the size of the influencer pool. Use this to understand how many unique people exist across all collaboration options.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of collaboration options (each is a proposed collaboration involving one or more influencers) that the ad team can choose from for the season.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific collaboration option (one candidate booking). Use this to refer to that particular collaboration when selecting the season lineup.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The influencers participating in this collaboration, given as space-separated influencer identifiers or names. When selecting collaborations, ensure no influencer listed here appears in more than one chosen collaboration.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct customers in the universe of stops that the dispatcher must consider when building tomorrow's plan. This counts all unique customer IDs referenced by the runs.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available delivery runs (routes) from which the dispatcher can select. The objective is to pick as many of these runs as possible without visiting any customer more than once.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single delivery run (e.g., an index or code). Use this to refer to a specific run when selecting which runs to include in the plan.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of customer IDs visited by that run. These are the stops for the run; any two selected runs must not share any of these customer IDs.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct children who appear in the sign-ups (the size of the universe of students). Helps understand how many unique child identifiers exist overall.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of after-school activity groups available to choose from (how many group rosters are listed).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this activity group (e.g., a label or number). Refers to the specific group you may choose to schedule.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated identifiers for the children enrolled in this group (the roster). When selecting groups for the schedule, no child_id listed here may appear in more than one chosen group.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct patrons (unique people) who appear across all proposed session sign-up lists — i.e., the size of the universe of patrons the librarian must avoid double-booking.

item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single proposed book discussion session (for example a code or name). Use this to refer to that entire session when deciding which sessions to run.

item_fields.name: elements

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct students in the school roster (the universe of people who might attend clubs). Used to know how many unique student identifiers exist for conflict checking.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: elements

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct consumer segments in the marketing universe — the complete set of segments that any campaign may target.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of targeted ad campaigns available for selection.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific ad campaign; used to refer to that campaign when deciding which campaigns to run.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated list of consumer segment identifiers that this campaign targets. When choosing campaigns to run, these target_segments must be pairwise disjoint so no segment is included in more than one selected campaign.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct staff (nurses and aides) on the hospital roster. This counts every unique staff ID that may appear in team rosters and defines the universe of personnel that must not be double-assigned.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed caregiver teams available to activate. This is how many team rosters follow and determines how many selection choices there are.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a proposed caregiver team (e.g., a number or label). Use this ID to reference and count teams when deciding which teams to activate.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated staff member IDs assigned to that team (members drawn from the total_staff_members pool). When selecting teams to activate, no staff ID listed here may appear in more than one selected team.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct landmarks across all excursions (the size of the universe). This tells you how many unique landmark identifiers exist that cannot be shared between chosen excursions.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of excursion options available to offer (the number of sets). Use this to know how many candidate guided tours you may choose from.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or name for this excursion (e.g., E1, 'OldTownWalk'). Refer to this when selecting which excursions to offer.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of landmark identifiers visited by this excursion. If this excursion is chosen, all listed landmarks become reserved and cannot appear in any other chosen excursion (no overlap allowed).

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct addresses (unique pickup locations) appearing across all suggested routes; this is the size of the universe of addresses that cannot be covered by more than one chosen route.

global_fields.name: num_sets

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single suggested pickup route (used to refer to that route when selecting or excluding it).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the addresses visited by this route; if two routes share any address from these lists, they conflict and at most one of them may be scheduled.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct instructors mentioned across all seminar proposals — the size of the instructor pool used to determine conflicts (no instructor may teach more than one approved seminar).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated instructor names or unique instructor IDs associated with that proposal. Any two proposals that share an instructor name/ID conflict and cannot both be approved.

global_fields.name: num_elements

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated donor identifiers that appear on this outreach list (e.g., email addresses or numeric IDs). When selecting lists to run, no donor_id listed here may appear on more than one chosen list.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct performers (artists) in the festival universe — i.e., the count of unique artists appearing across all listed band slots.

global_fields.name: num_elements

item_fields.name: elements

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct residents in the neighborhood (the size of the universe). This tells you how many unique resident IDs exist for validating group memberships.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredients across all appetizer platters. This is the size of the ingredient universe the planner must avoid duplicating among selected platters.

global_fields.name: num_elements

item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single candidate activity session (e.g., a label or number). Use this id to refer to that session when selecting which sessions to arrange.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of equipment item names (matching the universe of equipment). These are the specific pieces of gear that this activity needs; if this activity is arranged, none of these listed items may be used by any other arranged activity.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct authors in the pool of contributors. This counts every unique person who could appear in an issue and is used to understand the universe of authors that must not be duplicated across selected issues.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of themed issues (issue options) the magazine can choose from. The objective is to select as many of these as possible while ensuring no author contributes to more than one selected issue.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a specific themed issue (e.g., a number or label). Use this to refer to that issue when deciding which issues to publish.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of the authors who would contribute to this themed issue (names or author IDs). When choosing issues to publish, these contributor lists must be pairwise disjoint so that no author appears in more than one selected issue.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct garments (the universe of pieces) referenced across all capsule concepts. Use this to understand the size of the garment pool; each garment may appear in at most one produced capsule.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of capsule concepts (candidate collections) the buying team has proposed. The objective is to select as many of these capsule options as possible without any garment being used in more than one selected capsule.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single capsule concept (for example a name or code). Used to reference and count selected capsule collections.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: A space-separated list of garment identifiers (e.g., SKUs or piece names) that comprise this capsule. When choosing capsules to produce, no garment listed here may appear in more than one chosen capsule.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct book titles in the universe considered by the director (i.e., the count of unique titles that appear across all proposed book-club ideas). Used to understand the size of the title pool.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of club ideas the director sketched out (i.e., how many distinct proposed clubs/options are available to choose from).

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a single proposed book club (used to refer to that specific club idea when selecting which clubs to open).

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: The space-separated list of book titles proposed for that club (the exact titles that would be used if this club is opened). These titles must not overlap with titles of any other chosen club.

global_fields.name: num_elements
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct contractors available across all project proposals. This defines the universe of contractor identifiers that project proposals may reference.

global_fields.name: num_sets
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of project proposals submitted for approval. Each proposal is a candidate project (a set of contractors) and the goal is to approve as many of these as possible without assigning any contractor to more than one approved project.

item_fields.name: set_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this project proposal. Use this id when referring to, selecting, or listing approved projects in the final plan.

item_fields.name: elements
item_fields.scenario_description: Space-separated contractor identifiers required to complete this project. Each identifier must come from the contractor universe (num_contractors). Any two approved projects must not share any of these contractor identifiers.
